remedies.description: Implement a data enrichment step for location fields in the shipment notice generation process (DA-REJ) to ensure location data is complete and correct before notice creation.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: Can be done as a process change within the remaining 225 minutes; no external dependencies.
remedies.residual_gap: Does not address EVENT_ORDER rejections; location-related rejections (LOC_UNKNOWN) would be eliminated.

remedies.description: Add a pre-submit validation check in the handoff H-1 (ORG-A to ORG-B) that verifies location data presence and correctness, rejecting or correcting notices locally before transmission.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: Can be implemented as a validation rule in the existing handoff within the time window; no new tooling required.
remedies.residual_gap: Location-related rejections eliminated; EVENT_ORDER rejections may persist.

work_items.description: Enrich location data in carrier reject log
Validate location data before handoff H-1

output.rationale: E-01 shows two LOC_UNKNOWN rejections confirming missing location data as a root cause (H-ROOT-CAUSE-LOC-UNKNOWN). Enriching the data and validating before submit directly addresses this cause, while the stakeholder’s flakiness claim (E-02) remains unverified and does not obviate the need for correct location data. This aligns with the release scope and success criterion SC-SC1 targeting M-M1 (location-related reject rate). The work uses only the defined scope items; no catalog mutating tools are required as the steps are preparatory data improvements. Estimated effort fits within the remaining 200‑minute budget. Side‑effects include modest processing overhead during notice generation and handoff, which is reversible by disabling the enrichment/validation steps without altering existing data. An alternative of blindly resubmitting all rejected notices (per stakeholder suggestion) would not fix the underlying location defects and could increase carrier load, making it inferior to the proposed data‑centric approach.
